subject.title: feat: per-model code-mode capability flags with an "auto" master-switch tier

question: Should `tools.codeMode: "auto"` be accepted as a durable public configuration tier whose behavior is controlled by provider-owned `compat.codeMode: "preferred"` catalog metadata?
rationale: This is a new user-facing configuration contract and a cross-provider policy classification; tests can verify mechanics but cannot decide the permanent operator and catalog policy.

options.title: Accept the provider-owned auto tier
options.body: Keep the default `false`, land `"auto"` as an explicit opt-in tier, and treat preferred-model classifications as provider catalog policy.

options.title: Require explicit configuration instead
options.body: Keep the existing boolean-only contract and defer per-model activation until maintainers choose a different public selection model.

recommendation.title: Accept the provider-owned auto tier
recommendation.body: Keep the default `false`, land `"auto"` as an explicit opt-in tier, and treat preferred-model classifications as provider catalog policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied branch defines the feature’s intended public contract and provider catalog policy.
